Canadian Cyber Centre.title: AL26-029 - Critical vulnerability impacting Oracle Java - CVE-2026-114938
Canadian Cyber Centre.description:
Number: AL26-029
Date: November 17, 2026

Audience

This Alert is intended for IT professionals and managers.

Purpose

An Alert is used to raise awareness of a recently identified cyber threat that may impact cyber information assets, and to provide additional detection and mitigation advice to recipients. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security ("Cyber Centre") is also available to provide additional assistance regarding the content of this Alert to recipients as requested.

Details

The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre) is aware of a critical vulnerability affecting Java runtimesFootnote 1.

Tracked as CVE-2026-114938Footnote 2, this vulnerability is classified as a Heap-based Buffer Overflow [CWE-122]Footnote 3 that affects the Base64 standard Java library. Known as “Java4Shell”, the vulnerability could be exploited remotely without authentication by sending specially crafted base64 data to Java processes running on x86-64 processors that contain AVX-512 Vector Byte Manipulation Instructions (VBMI) hardware. Successful exploitation could result in memory corruption, disclosure of sensitive information, process crashes or arbitrary code execution in affected applications or services.

Oracle has released a security advisory addressing this vulnerabilityFootnote 4. Organizations should identify affected systems and apply applicable vendor updates as soon as they become available.

The Cyber Centre is not aware of active exploitation at this time, but that can change quickly.

Suggested actions

The Cyber Centre strongly recommends that organizations identify affected Java applications and update vulnerable components to an appropriate fixed release:

Affected Products Affected Versions Fixed Version
Oracle Java SE 8 8u511b33-perf 8u513-perf
Oracle Java SE 17 Versions 17.0.6 prior to or equal to 17.0.21.0.3 17.0.21.1
Oracle Java SE 21 Versions 21.0.13.0.3 and prior 21.0.13.1
Oracle Java SE 25 Versions 25.0.5.0.3 and prior 25.0.5.1
Oracle Java SE 27 Versions 27.0.1.0.3 and prior 27.0.1.1
Oracle GraalVM for JDK Versions 17.0.6 prior to or equal to 17.0.21.0.3 AND versions 21.0.0 prior to or equal to 21.0.13.0.3 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1
Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition Versions 21.3.20.0.3 and prior 21.3.20.1
Oracle OpenJDK Versions 17.0.6 prior to or equal to 27.0.1.0.3 27.0.1.1

For further details on affected versions and available fixed releases, please refer to the following Oracle advisoryFootnote 4.

The Cyber Centre recommends that organizations:

  • Inventory Java Environments. Audit all applications to identify active Java runtimes, including vendor, full build versionFootnote 5.
  • Update affected Java installations immediately to a fixed, supported release.
  • Prioritize Internet-facing systems and applications.
  • Identify third-party products, appliances and containers that include vulnerable Java componentsFootnote 6.
  • Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix can be applied.
  • Consider disabling JVM support for AVX-512 by using JVM flag -XX:UseAVX=2 if you cannot patch.
  • To determine if your processor supports AVX-512, the following instructions can be used on Linux: lscpu | grep avx512.
  • Monitor for potential compromise by reviewing web server, application, authentication, and endpoint logs for suspicious activity.
  • Continuously monitor third-party vendors for security updates, including appliances, applications and services that bundle Java, and apply applicable patches without delay.

Organizations should also review the Cyber Centre’s Top 10 IT Security ActionsFootnote 7.

Should activity matching the content of this alert be discovered, recipients are encouraged to report via My Cyber Portal, or email contact@cyber.gc.ca.

Microsoft Security Update Guide.description: Missing release of memory after effective lifetime in Windows Layer-2 Bridge Network Driver allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service over an adjacent network.

Microsoft Security Update Guide.description: Out-of-bounds read in Remote Desktop Client allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

Microsoft Security Update Guide.description: Heap-based buffer overflow in SQL Server allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: Microsoft named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for SIEM
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
We're honored that Microsoft has once again been recognized as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Security Information and Event Management (SIEM).

The post Microsoft named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for SIEM  appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: Security for the agentic era, powered by Microsoft Perception
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
Read about updates to Microsoft Perception and the new Microsoft Security cyber stack to defend against threats, secure agents, and protect your digital estate.

The post Security for the agentic era, powered by Microsoft Perception  appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: The risks of device code authentication for AI coding agents
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
Lab research shows how device code phishing, a technique that applies to any device-flow client, can extend to AI coding agents, using GitHub Copilot CLI as an illustrative example.

The post The risks of device code authentication for AI coding agents appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: High volume phishing campaign uses Microsoft 365 outage lures to target multiple industry sectors
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence observed a high-volume phishing campaign using Microsoft 365 outage-themed lures to target organizations across multiple sectors worldwide.

The post High volume phishing campaign uses Microsoft 365 outage lures to target multiple industry sectors appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: SCKit abuses ScreenConnect to deploy remote access and target technician sessions
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
SCKit abuses ScreenConnect to deploy unauthorized remote access and target technicians. Explore the attack chain, mitigations, and Microsoft Defender XDR hunting.

The post SCKit abuses ScreenConnect to deploy remote access and target technician sessions appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: Trained to betray: How post-training supply chain attacks hijack coding agents
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
Microsoft Defender Research and the AI Red Team discuss how poisoned datasets and poisoned model checkpoints can trigger remote code execution and other malicious activities.

The post Trained to betray: How post-training supply chain attacks hijack coding agents appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: The global socket: how threat actors are weaponizing GSocket for stealthy C2
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
Threat actors are deploying GSocket on compromised Linux servers to keep encrypted remote access after the original vulnerability is patched. Learn how to detect, investigate, and remediate this activity.

The post The global socket: how threat actors are weaponizing GSocket for stealthy C2 appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: Lessons from 59 Linux Kernel Bug Reports
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
Microsoft FORGE Lab researchers used codename MDASH to investigate Linux kernel vulnerabilities, resulting in 59 upstream bug reports, 33 assigned CVEs, and 38 merged fixes. The research includes eight demonstrated local root privilege-escalation exploits and examines the challenges of turning AI-generated findings into validated vulnerabilities and upstream fixes.

The post Lessons from 59 Linux Kernel Bug Reports appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: Detecting sleeper agents hiding in AI model neurons
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
Microsoft Research has released new threat research detailing how a capable agent model could be turned into a sleeper agent by editing fewer than ten neurons to inject a short payload; Microsoft Research has also found that this threat is detectable by frontier agents, which can identify anomalous weight edits.

The post Detecting sleeper agents hiding in AI model neurons appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: FORGE Lab uses agentic tools to identify memory safety issues in Rust
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
Microsoft FORGE Lab researchers found memory-safety bugs in Rust's core and std libraries, including cases where safe Rust code can trigger undefined behavior. Using Hyenas, FORGE's frontier research version of codename MDASH, the team investigated three patterns of misplaced trust in unsafe code and what they reveal about Rust's safety guarantees.

The post FORGE Lab uses agentic tools to identify memory safety issues in Rust appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: ARTEX abuse expands as cybercriminals target financial sector
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
In October 2026, the financially motivated threat actor Storm-3358 began targeting organizations in the financial sector using the agentic AI offensive framework ARTEX.

The post ARTEX abuse expands as cybercriminals target financial sector appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence has observed threat actors using the agentic offensive security framework ARTEX to search GitHub for OAuth application secrets, which can be used to compromise the associated OAuth application and perform authenticated actions in the application’s tenant. Agents operating on behalf of threat actors then used the compromised OAuth applications to perform a variety of subsequent actions within compromised organizations.

The post Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: New investments to reduce on-premises security risk
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
We’re announcing a new on-premises security initiative, bringing together guidance, migration, and product investments.

The post New investments to reduce on-premises security risk appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: ​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: November 2026
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
Microsoft Security’s November 2026 updates strengthen AI agent security, least privilege, threat protection, and exposure management.

The post ​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: November 2026 appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

Microsoft Security Blog.title: Email threat landscape: Q3 2026 trends and insights
Microsoft Security Blog.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence observed a sharp rise in email-based phishing activity at the end of Q3 2026 (July – September), even as QR code phishing declined, CAPTCHA-gated phishing recovered, and malicious messages spoofing familiar business-service sender domains exposed risks associated with security overrides.

The post Email threat landscape: Q3 2026 trends and insights appeared first on Microsoft Security Blog.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-95619
CVE.report.description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. An integer overflow can occur when processing large inputs to the aligned operator new in the C++ library. This vulnerability could lead to an undersized memory allocation, potentially causing memory corruption or application instability.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-94451
CVE.report.description: Quarkus REST Data Panache provides a way to automatically generate REST endpoints for data entities. A flaw was found where certain endpoints do not properly check the sort parameter provided by users. This could allow an attacker to learn information they should not have access to or slow down the system by forcing the database to perform complex tasks, potentially causing a denial of service.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-93432
CVE.report.description: A flaw was found in the Quarkus Qute template engine. When the {#eval} section helper processes a sub-template, it fails to pass the parent template's content type information. This bypasses standard escaping mechanisms, allowing untrusted data to be output as raw, unescaped text. This vulnerability can lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and JSON Injection, potentially allowing a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code in a user's browser or manipulate data.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129814
CVE.report.description: The SDO Information Get Object Description and Get Entry Description responses copy the object or entry name into the mailbox data area and then write a null terminator byte. The copy loops ran up to the last available byte in the buffer, leaving no room for the terminator. When an object or entry name exactly fills the available space the terminator is written one byte past the end of the mailbox data buffer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129813
CVE.report.description: The CoE complete-access download handler iterated over all subindices of an object and wrote the master-supplied payload into each writable entry. Entries that hold a constant have write-access flags set but carry a NULL data pointer. The handler did not check for this and wrote the master payload through the NULL pointer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129812
CVE.report.description: An object dictionary entry that holds a constant has no process data storage and carries a NULL data pointer. sizeOfPDO did not check for this when resolving a mapped entry to its descriptor. A master that maps such an entry to a PDO causes COE_pdoPack or COE_pdoUnpack to dereference the NULL data pointer on every process data exchange after the mapping is activated.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129811
CVE.report.description: The PDO mapping bit lengths stored in the mapping objects are writable by the master via SDO. sizeOfPDO summed them without checking the total against the size of the rxpdo[] or txpdo[] process data buffers. A master can craft a mapping whose total bit count exceeds those buffers, causing COE_pdoPack and COE_pdoUnpack to write past their ends during each process data cycle after the PREOP to SAFEOP transition.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129810
CVE.report.description: ESC_eoeprocess and ESC_eoeprocess_tx can be reached before the application calls EOE_config to supply the callback table pointer. When eoe_cfg is NULL the receive handler dereferenced it while processing an incoming EoE frame, and the transmit polling function dereferenced it on each cycle, causing NULL pointer dereferences.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129809
CVE.report.description: ESC_foeprocess can be reached by an incoming mailbox frame before the application calls FOE_config to supply the file table and flush buffer pointers. When foe_cfg or its fbuffer field is NULL the handler dereferenced those pointers while processing the frame, causing a NULL pointer dereference.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129808
CVE.report.description: The EoE receive and transmit paths call the handle_recv_buffer and fetch_send_buffer callbacks without first checking whether they are set. Both callbacks are documented as optional; an application that omits either one causes a call through a NULL function pointer when the first EoE frame arrives or when the transmit polling loop runs.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129807
CVE.report.description: The FoE file table allows entries to omit a write handler by setting write_function to NULL, making the file read-only. FOE_fopen did not check whether write_function was present before accepting a write request; a master sending a WRQ for a read-only file caused a call through a NULL function pointer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129806
CVE.report.description: The CoE SDO upload handler enters its normal-response path (used for objects longer than 4 bytes) and passes (objd + nsub)->data directly to the pre-object handler and to the response copy. Entries that hold a constant in the value field have data set to NULL; a master can request such an entry and cause a NULL pointer dereference in the upload path.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129805
CVE.report.description: An object dictionary entry can carry write-access flags and still have a NULL data pointer, for example when a constant value is held in the value field rather than in addressable storage. The CoE SDO download handler checked write access but not whether storage was present, then wrote the master-supplied payload through the NULL pointer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129804
CVE.report.description: FOE_read and FOE_write store the filename length as uint8_t, truncating it modulo 256. When (mbxheader.length - ESC_FOEHSIZE) is a multiple of 256, the length becomes 0. Additionally, a request whose mailbox length equals ESC_FOEHSIZE exactly also produces a length of 0 without any truncation. In both cases FOE_fopen calls strncmp with a length of 0, which always returns equal, so the first registered file whose password is 0 is opened regardless of the filename the master sent.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129803
CVE.report.description: The CoE entry gate accepts frames with mbxheader.length as low as COE_MINIMUM_LENGTH (8), but a normal SDO Download requires at least COE_HEADERSIZE (10) bytes of CoE payload to carry its header fields. With mbxheader.length of 8 or 9, the segmented-transfer branch misevaluates due to unsigned wrap, leaving the declared SDO size unclamped. copy2mbx then reads that many bytes starting past the end of the actual payload and writes them into the object buffer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129802
CVE.report.description: EOE_set_ip reads each network parameter field (MAC, IP, subnet, gateway, DNS IP, DNS name) from the mailbox payload before checking whether the payload is large enough to contain them. The single bounds check at the end of the function does not prevent the reads from happening. A master can send a Set-IP frame with all flags set and mbxheader.length equal to the minimum, causing all reads to access memory past the end of the payload.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129801
CVE.report.description: The FoE DATA frame handler computes the payload length from the master-supplied mailbox length field and passes it directly to FOE_fwrite. The length is checked against the remaining file capacity but not against the physical mailbox buffer size. A master can declare a large length while sending a short frame, causing FOE_fwrite to read past the end of the mailbox buffer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129800
CVE.report.description: sizeOfPDO, called during state transitions, uses the subindex-0 count of the SM-assign and PDO-mapping objects as loop bounds without checking those counts against the descriptor array sizes. On builds where those subindex-0 values are writable via SDO, a master can write 0xFF and cause sizeOfPDO to read past the end of the descriptor arrays on the next transition to SAFEOP.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129799
CVE.report.description: A CoE SDO request for index 0xFFFF matches the object list terminator entry instead of returning not-found. The terminator has a NULL objdesc pointer. Callers dereference it without checking, crashing the slave.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129798
CVE.report.description: The CoE SDO segmented download handler advances a write pointer by each incoming segment's size but does not track how many bytes have been written in total. A master can keep sending non-last segments until the pointer has walked past the end of the object buffer or the complete-access staging buffer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129797
CVE.report.description: SDO_downloadsegment is called whenever a mailbox frame carries the DOWNLOADSEGREQ command byte, regardless of whether a segmented download is actually in progress. ESCvar.data, which the handler writes through, is NULL until a segmented transfer is started. A master can send a DOWNLOADSEGREQ at any time and write through a NULL or stale pointer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129796
CVE.report.description: The CoE SDO download handler for flexible-length objects (VISIBLE_STRING, OCTET_STRING, and similar) does not check that the master-declared transfer size fits within the object before writing. Two distinct writes are affected: the VISIBLE_STRING zero-padding memset and the first-frame copy into the object buffer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129795
CVE.report.description: When the last EoE fragment has the TIME_APPEND flag set, the handler subtracts 4 from rxframeoffset to strip the timestamp. There is no check that rxframeoffset is at least 4. A fragment carrying fewer than 4 bytes of payload that is also marked LAST causes rxframeoffset to wrap to 0xFFFFFFFC, which is then stored as the buffer length and handed to the TCP/IP stack.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129794
CVE.report.description: The EoE fragment reassembly code uses a frame size from the wire as the bound for memcpy into the application receive buffer, without checking that the declared size fits in the actual buffer. A master can write up to 2016 bytes into a buffer the application may have sized much smaller.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130323
CVE.report.description: The Accept Stripe Payments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'href of any <a> element containing 'asp_action=show_pp&product_id='' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.1.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that a user clicks the attacker-placed comment link to trigger the sink; however, if the non-default 'Prefetch Payment Popup Scripts' option is enabled, execution occurs on page load with no user interaction required.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-126705
CVE.report.description: The WP Job Portal – AI-Powered Recruitment System for Company or Job Board website plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based SQL Injection via the 'columns[<attacker-chosen key>]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.0 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-124976
CVE.report.description: The Swift Performance Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '<attacker-chosen parameter name>' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.3.7.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires that an administrator has configured at least one Cacheable AJAX Action via the plugin's AJAX Cache feature, a condition attackers can confirm by probing for a swift-performance: HIT response header.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-124248
CVE.report.description: The GPTranslate – Multilingual AI Translation Agent for WordPress: Translate Your Site with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.34.17 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the plugin's non-default 'HTML DOM method' to be enabled for server-side translation, and a translation row for the target language-prefixed URL must exist to arm the output buffer that routes page content through the vulnerable Simple HTML DOM parser.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-124216
CVE.report.description: The Orphans plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.4.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires a two-step comment chain: a benign first comment must be approved under a given name and email so that WordPress's comment_previously_approved mechanism auto-publishes the attacker's payload comment without moderation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-123970
CVE.report.description: The wpForo Forum plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'thread[body]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.2.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful execution of the injected script is limited to viewers whose forum access profile denies attachment viewing (va=0 or caa=0), meaning exploitation depends on an administrator having configured a custom forum access profile that permits reading but denies attachment viewing — this is not the default shipped configuration.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-123830
CVE.report.description: The wpForo Forum plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[display_name]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.2.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires public user registration to be enabled (users_can_register=1) and a valid _wpfnonce fetched from the public sign-up page, but is otherwise fully unauthenticated.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-122264
CVE.report.description: The wpForo Forum plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'member[about]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.2.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the attacking subscriber to have met the default antispam threshold of at least 3 forum posts before the account editing page becomes accessible.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-122228
CVE.report.description: The ProfilePress – Paid Membership, Online Courses (LMS), Ecommerce, User Registration & Login Form, User Profile & Restrict Content plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 4.18.0 via the 'sortby<form_id>, filter<form_id>' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract reconstruct any listed member's full e-mail address one character at a time via a boolean LIKE oracle, and enumerate users holding arbitrary usermeta keys such as ppress_billing_phone. The e-mail address oracle is reachable on any default install that used the plugin's 'Create pages' onboarding notice, because pp_email_address is enabled as a search field by default and the resulting directory page is published with no capability or nonce gate.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120745
CVE.report.description: The Paid Membership Plugin, Ecommerce, User Registration Form, Login Form, User Profile & Restrict Content – ProfilePress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'reg_bio' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.18.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The reg_bio parameter is accepted by the registration handler's allowlist even when the rendered registration form does not include a biography field, meaning an unauthenticated attacker can supply the payload via a raw POST request without needing a visible biography input on the form.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120736
CVE.report.description: The AutomatorWP – No-Code Workflow Automation, Integration & Webhooks Plugin, now with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'your-message (any CF7 form field used in a form_field: tag)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.0.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to have configured a public 'Guest submits a form' automation whose Send-an-email action embeds a form_field tag, after which the payload fires the next time any user opens the affected automation's email log entry.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-119177
CVE.report.description: The Real Cookie Banner: GDPR & ePrivacy Cookie Consent plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.4.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the cookie banner has been activated by the site administrator (the plugin's primary onboarding step) and that at least one prior comment from the same name and email identity has already been approved, after which WordPress core's comment_previously_approved default auto-approves subsequent comments without administrator action.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-119157
CVE.report.description: The PublishPress Capabilities: User Role Access Control, Admin Area Permissions plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'page_elements' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.53.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires an administrator to open a Profile Features capture window and save at least one of the attacker-supplied rows on the Profile Features screen, which represents the ordinary documented use of the feature and leaves no visible indication to the administrator that malicious data was submitted.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116518
CVE.report.description: The ElasticPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'orderby' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected payload is stored in the ep_query_log transient for up to 24 hours after a single unauthenticated frontend GET request, and only fires when an administrator subsequently opens the Status Report page and expands the Failed Queries panel.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-109196
CVE.report.description: The FV Player 8 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data.videos[].fv_wp_flowplayer_field_splash' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.1.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The wp_ajax_fv_player_db_save handler's ownership and capability check is conditional on the presence of the data.update field; omitting it bypasses authorization entirely, allowing a Subscriber-level attacker to overwrite any existing video record using an enumerable video ID — and the valid nonce required by the endpoint is issued to every logged-in visitor of any page hosting the publicly accessible [fvplayer_editor] shortcode.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-107771
CVE.report.description: The Speed Booster Pack ⚡ PageSpeed Optimization Suite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the plugin's Lazy load media option is enabled and that the attacker's comment is approved by a site administrator or via auto-approval.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-107747
CVE.report.description: The WP Custom Admin Interface plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'first_name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.43 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-107654
CVE.report.description: The One to one user Chat by WPGuppy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'userId' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.6 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The plugin's permission callback is trivially bypassed because it validates a JWT that the plugin itself signs using an attacker-supplied value from the guppy_guest_account cookie, and the guest code path (userType=0) skips the get_userdata() check that would confirm the userId corresponds to a real WordPress user.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-17591
CVE.report.description: A flaw was found in libarchive. An attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or potential information disclosure due to a use-after-free vulnerability, which occurs when a program reads memory that has already been released. This issue arises when the archive_entry_copy_mac_metadata() function deallocates an internal buffer before completing a data copy. An attacker who can supply input to an application utilizing this function can trigger the flaw to crash the application or read uninitialized memory data.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129344
CVE.report.description:
Uncaught Exception vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix allows an unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service via a client-selected legacy serializer on binary channel broadcasts.

When an application broadcasts {:binary, data} payloads on a channel topic, any client that connects without a vsn parameter, or with vsn=1.0.0, and joins that topic makes those broadcasts fail. Phoenix.Channel.Server.send/4 encodes each broadcast with every subscriber's own serializer inside the PubSub dispatch loop, calling fastlane!/1 with no rescue, and the negotiated Phoenix.Socket.V1.JSONSerializer raises Protocol.UndefinedError on a binary payload. Every binary broadcast on the topic then crashes the broadcasting process and skips every subscriber dispatched after the attacker. For broadcasts arriving from other nodes the loop runs in the PubSub adapter worker, whose repeated crashes restart the PubSub supervisor and empty the node's subscription registry while sockets stay connected.

This issue affects phoenix: from 1.5.7 before 1.5.16, from 1.6.0-rc.0 before 1.6.18, from 1.7.0-rc.0 before 1.7.25, and from 1.8.0-rc.0 before 1.8.17.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-128361
CVE.report.description:
Improper Input Validation vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix (Phoenix.Presence) allows an attacker who can join a channel to cause a denial of service via a non-string presence key.

track/3,4 accepts any term as the presence key, such as a JSON object taken from a join payload. The key is converted with to_string/1 only later, in Phoenix.Presence.group/1, which raises Protocol.UndefinedError on a map. group/1 runs whenever presences are listed and when each presence diff is broadcast, together with the application's fetch/2, which can likewise raise on an unexpected key. Once such a key is tracked, every process that lists presences on the topic crashes, typically each channel that joins it, and presence diffs for the topic are lost.

From 1.7.0 the diff runs in a Task.Supervisor.async task linked to the tracker shard, and Phoenix.Presence.handle_info/2 has no clause for its failure. The shard then terminates, taking down every channel and LiveView process tracked on it and erasing presence state for all its topics. Repeated joins exhaust the restart intensity and take down the application supervisor.

This issue affects phoenix: from 1.2.0 before 1.5.16, from 1.6.0-rc.0 before 1.6.18, from 1.7.0-rc.0 before 1.7.25, and from 1.8.0-rc.0 before 1.8.17.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2022-4998
CVE.report.description: A vulnerability was identified in kanishka-linux reminiscence 0.3 on Windows. This issue affects the function convert_html_pdf_with_chromium of the file pages/dbaccess.py of the component Chromium HTML-to-PDF Conversion Pipeline. Such manipulation of the argument url_name leads to os command injection. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-133964
CVE.report.description: A security vulnerability has been detected in Bytebase DBHub up to 2.0.0. Impacted is the function escapeHatchFunctionKeywords of the file src/utils/allowed-keywords.ts of the component Read Only Mode. The manipulation of the argument tool leads to incomplete blacklist. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-133367
CVE.report.description: The WPC Frequently Bought Together for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'variation' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.0.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The nonce protecting the woobt_add_all_to_cart AJAX handler is emitted to all unauthenticated visitors via wp_localize_script, effectively nullifying the nonce as an authentication barrier and making the handler reachable without any login.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131609
CVE.report.description: The Germanized for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'billing_address.first_name (Store API checkout) → stored on parent order; withdrawal get_first_name() fallback' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.1.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload is planted via an unauthenticated guest checkout order's billing first name through the WooCommerce Store API, with execution triggered by a subsequent unauthenticated withdrawal request submission whose nonce is publicly available on the /withdraw-from-contract/ page.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-127133
CVE.report.description: The Stream – Activity Log & Audit Trail plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'group-name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires BuddyPress to be active with its Groups component enabled and default group-creation permissions in place, allowing any logged-in member to create groups.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-124214
CVE.report.description: The WP Data Access – App Builder for Tables, Forms, Dashboards, Charts & Maps plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HyperlinkObject.label (percent-encoded)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.5.92 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the WordPress site to have a published Anonymous-access Registration Form app configured against a table with a HyperlinkObject column, and a legacy Data Project list using a $$link$$ Dynamic Hyperlink against that same column; given this configuration, any unauthenticated visitor can plant the payload.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-122230
CVE.report.description: The Thim Kit for Elementor – Pre-built Templates & Widgets for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the Post Comment widget is used with the Text Reveal entrance animation (Elementor class 'ekit--fx-word-reveal') on a Single Post template, and the comment widget must be within the initial viewport; once the first comment by an attacker is approved, or if comment moderation is disabled, subsequent payloads fire automatically for every visitor who loads the affected page.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120743
CVE.report.description: The Simply Schedule Appointments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'payment_method' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.13.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The stored payload is only rendered when an administrator navigates to the hidden support page (/wp-admin/admin.php?ssa-support-admin=1) and triggers the 'Fix appointment durations' action, a condition reliably engineered by the attacker by smuggling a '+1 day' suffix in the start_date field to create a persistent duration mismatch that routes the malicious booking through the vulnerable echo path. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120526
CVE.report.description: The WCFM Membership – WooCommerce Memberships for Multivendor Marketplace plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'wcfm_membership_registration_form[store_name]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.12.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The nonce required to reach the registration endpoint is publicly emitted on the /vendor-register/ page, making the endpoint fully reachable by unauthenticated attackers without any prior authentication or privilege escalation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120119
CVE.report.description: The HUSKY – Products Filter for WooCommerce Professional plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based SQL Injection via the 'link (inner 'woof_text' query parameter)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.7 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The exploit requires a valid product_messenger nonce, which is issued by the woof_redraw_woof AJAX endpoint to any visitor when the shortcode's by_only attribute is set — an attribute that can itself be forced via the attacker-controlled woof_shortcode request parameter, making the nonce trivially obtainable by any logged-in user.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-87092
CVE.report.description: The Unlimited Elements For Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.26 via the getFileContentByUrl function. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. The nonce protecting the get_addon_output_data AJAX endpoint is emitted on the Elementor editor page, which is accessible to Contributors, making the endpoint reachable by any authenticated user at that privilege level or above.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-119608
CVE.report.description: The Hustle – Email Marketing, Lead Generation, Optins, Popups plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'import_file' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.8.14.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to have first delegated the hustle_edit_module capability to a lower-privileged role via the plugin's built-in Permissions screen; without that delegation, the import endpoint rejects non-Administrator users at the capability check.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-119216
CVE.report.description: The Stream – Activity Log & Audit Trail plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'display_name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.4.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is only exploitable on sites with 50 or fewer total users, as above that threshold the user filter uses an AJAX endpoint that returns entity-encoded labels and is not affected.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-119114
CVE.report.description: The WP Fastest Cache – WordPress Cache Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary directory deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the singleDeleteCache function in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Successful exploitation requires either the Custom Permalinks plugin or the GeoDirectory plugin to be co-installed, as these provide the necessary mechanism to write a traversal-bearing permalink value into the database that WP Fastest Cache then consumes without validation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-119061
CVE.report.description: The VikBooking Hotel Booking Engine & PMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'vbf<field_id>' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.20 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118061
CVE.report.description: The VikBooking Hotel Booking Engine & PMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'inquiry (array keys)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.20 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The endpoint's only access gate is a CSRF token that is publicly emitted on the unauthenticated inquiry page, making the injection reachable by any unauthenticated visitor without any precondition beyond loading that public page.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118049
CVE.report.description: The Tutor LMS – eLearning and online course solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.0 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to permanently delete any comment they authored anywhere on the site — including regular post comments and lesson comments — along with all replies to those comments authored by any other user, including Administrators and Instructors.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116757
CVE.report.description: The Tutor LMS – eLearning and online course solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '_tutor_profile_bio' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected anchor payload uses a full-viewport invisible overlay (position:fixed; width:100vw; height:100vh; opacity:0) so that any click on the public profile page triggers the tutor-copy-text handler, which passes a browser-decoded data-text value to tutor_toast() where it is parsed as live HTML by jQuery.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-107632
CVE.report.description: The Unbounce Landing Pages plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.1.6. This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on the proxy error message that is persisted to the 'ub-proxy-error-message' option: unauthenticated attacker-controlled REQUEST_URI data is concatenated into the error string in UBHTTP::stream_request_curl()/stream_request_wp_remote() and stored via update_option(), then later echoed inside a <textarea> on the Unbounce Pages Diagnostics admin page without any escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user (an administrator viewing the Diagnostics screen) accesses an injected page.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-104013
CVE.report.description: The WP Compress – Instant Performance & Speed Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Directory Traversal in all versions up to, and including, 7.26.00 via the 'css' parameter parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read the contents of arbitrary files on the server, which can contain sensitive information. Exploiting the file read requires a preparatory unauthenticated request that plants a boundary directory by injecting a path traversal sequence into a cookie listed in WPC_CACHE_COOKIES (such as pll_language, present in the default list), meaning the plugin's cookie-cache feature must be enabled with at least one tracked cookie name configured.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-133963
CVE.report.description: A vulnerability was determined in MaysWind AriaNg-Native up to 1.3.14. Affected by this issue is the function shell.openPath of the file main/ipc/main-process.js of the component IPC Handler. This manipulation of the argument dir causes improper input validation. The attack can be initiated remotely. Upgrading to version 1.3.15 can resolve this issue. Patch name: ac5a4bcf102f605b160f19fcc9fbaec67f9596d7. You should upgrade the affected component.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-125054
CVE.report.description: The SiteOrigin CSS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'class' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires a Contributor-level or higher attacker to store a crafted class attribute value in a post, which then fires when a user with the edit_theme_options capability opens the Visual Inspector on the affected post and clicks anywhere in the preview iframe. Exploitation by unauthenticated attackers requires that a third-party plugin providing wp_kses_post()-filtered unauthenticated front-end submission is installed and configured, and a moderator approves the submission. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with contributor-level access and above.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-133369
CVE.report.description: The CodePeople Post Map for Google Maps plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'cpm_map[api_key]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The settings form nonce is itself rendered on the Subscriber-accessible page (reachable via a trailing-slash bypass of the slug guard), making nonce verification no real barrier to the unauthorized save.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-133361
CVE.report.description: The BlockStrap Page Builder – Bootstrap Blocks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 0.1.65 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that the attacker has previously had at least one comment approved for a given name and email address, allowing subsequent comments from that author to bypass moderation under WordPress's default policy; exploitation is also limited to sites using a block theme, which is the WordPress default.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132620
CVE.report.description: The WPBot – AI ChatBot for WordPress & Growth Suite: SEO, AI Writer, Email Marketing, Social Media plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'text' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit is triggered when an administrator opens the Chat Sessions screen, at which point the plugin's bundled Bootstrap 3.3.7 affix data-API passes the attacker-controlled data-target attribute value to jQuery as HTML, executing the injected script in the administrator's session.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131822
CVE.report.description: The Contact Form to Any API plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'your-message (any CF7 form field)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.0.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The malicious payload is stored via a single unauthenticated POST to Contact Form 7's public REST feedback endpoint, which uses permission_callback __return_true and requires no authentication or prior interaction to submit.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130150
CVE.report.description: The Product Import Export for WooCommerce – CSV Product Importer & Exporter plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author (initial store via wp-comments-post.php) / CSV cell on import' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.6.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit requires an administrator to approve the attacker's review, then export and re-import it using the plugin's default column mapping, with the import taking the INSERT branch — which occurs automatically on any site whose database table prefix is not the literal 'wp_', when the CSV has no comment_ID mapping, or when the original review has been trashed. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-126011
CVE.report.description: The Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the site administrator to have configured the Thickbox lightbox effect with the "Try to apply to all images" context (thumbEffectContext=all_images), and exploitation additionally depends on an administrator approving the attacker's initial comment so that subsequent comments from that author are auto-approved.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-125039
CVE.report.description: The EZ SQL Reports Shortcode Widget and DB Backup plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'User-Agent header (stored to comment_agent)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.26.45 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that an administrator has saved a report whose SQL query selects attacker-controlled data such as comment_agent, and that the attacker can identify the saved report's slug — a condition trivially met when the administrator publishes the report on a public page via the [SQLREPORT] shortcode.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120738
CVE.report.description: The Organize Media Folder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'EXIF.DateTimeOriginal' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.00 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This bypass of wp_filter_post_kses means the injected payload survives regardless of the uploader's unfiltered_html capability; Subscriber-level access becomes sufficient when a front-end attachment-upload integration such as bbPress with forumAttachments is active, and exploitation requires no special configuration because the %created_timestamp% placeholder is included in the caption template by default. Exploitation by attackers with subscriber-level access and above requires that bbPress and gd-bbpress-attachments (forumAttachments) are installed and configured so that Subscribers/Participants can post attachments through a frontend forum form. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with author-level access and above.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120679
CVE.report.description: The Redux Framework plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '<opt_name>[<color-field-id>]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.17 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The wp_kses_post() sanitization applied via Redux_Helpers::sanitize_array() is bypassed — not broken — because an &lt;a class="thickbox" title="&amp;lt;img onerror=...&amp;gt;"&gt; payload uses only kses-allowed tags and attributes, with the entity-encoded onerror handler surviving storage as inert text that the browser decodes when WordPress core's thickbox.js reads the title attribute and writes it into the modal as HTML. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120676
CVE.report.description: The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'upload-1 (the File Upload field's element_id)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is an incomplete fix for CVE-2024-1794; exploitation requires that the Forminator form's File Upload field is left at plugin defaults (no 'custom-files' restriction configured) and that the server maps no Content-Type to the .rtx extension — the default behavior of the Debian/Ubuntu Apache package used by the official WordPress Docker image and many shared hosts.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120529
CVE.report.description: The Admin Columns plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The kses sanitization pass in classes/Sanitize/Kses.php uses wp_kses_allowed_html('post') augmented with iframe[src] and the data: protocol; because wp_kses_attr_check accepts any data-* attribute on any allowed tag without inspecting its value, a payload embedded inside a data-ac-tip attribute survives intact and is subsequently assigned to innerHTML by assets/js/table.js, bypassing the apparent mitigation entirely.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120486
CVE.report.description: The ShortPixel Image Optimizer – Optimize Images, Convert WebP & AVIF plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.6.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the administrator to have enabled the 'Deliver WebP/AVIF images using the ShortPixel CDN' (useCDN) option, after which any unauthenticated visitor can submit a comment containing a crafted url() payload inside an allowed HTML construct such as <acronym title="...">, which WordPress comment kses preserves on save; the dangerous attribute-boundary breakout occurs only at render time inside the ob_start output-buffer rewriter, where kses does not apply.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120485
CVE.report.description: The Admin Columns plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'url' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has added the Author URL column to the Comments screen layout and that the site accepts unauthenticated comments, both of which are default WordPress and plugin configurations.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-119632
CVE.report.description: The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'textarea-N (rich-text draft value, saved as Save-and-Continue draft meta)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the targeted form to have a Rich-Text Textarea field with Save-and-Continue enabled and public submission permissions — once a crafted draft is saved, the payload executes whenever any user, including an administrator, resumes the draft or opens the Draft ID link from the Forminator Submissions screen.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118059
CVE.report.description: The MailerLite – Signup forms (official) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'form_id' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.27 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to approve a comment containing the malicious shortcode, after which any page rendering the Latest Comments block with excerpts enabled will trigger the injected script for all visitors.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116619
CVE.report.description: The MetForm – Contact Form, Survey, Quiz, Conditional Forms, Form Templates & Custom Form Builder for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'mf-te (the form-builder-chosen name of the Text Editor field)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires a published form containing a Text Editor block; the form's public markup exposes the submission nonce as data-form-nonce, allowing any unauthenticated visitor to satisfy the only submission barrier and store the malicious payload.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-107713
CVE.report.description: The Flutterwave Payments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'form_id' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The storing endpoint is accessible without authentication because the required nonce is publicly exposed on any front-end page rendering the plugin's [flw-pay-form], [flw-pay-button], or [flw-donation-form] shortcodes, allowing any unauthenticated visitor to scrape and reuse it.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-104904
CVE.report.description: The Shortcodes Ultimate plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in versions up to, and including, 7.9.1 This is due to su_get_current_url() interpolating the raw Host request header into the authority portion of a URL that is then passed to esc_url() — which by design preserves '[' and ']' inside the authority so IPv6 literal hosts remain valid — and the [su_qrcode] shortcode substituting that value into its data attribute (the documented %CURRENT_URL% token) before feeding it to do_shortcode(). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include arbitrary PHP files that reside within the active theme's root directory (bounded because '/' inside an attribute value terminates parse_url()'s host and is then percent-encoded and stripped), and — when the shipped-default 'Unsafe features' option remains on — to read arbitrary post meta of any post, on any front-end page that renders [su_qrcode data="%CURRENT_URL%"].

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-96991
CVE.report.description: The SchemaEngine AI – AI Schema Markup, Reviews & Rich Snippets for SEO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content via WebPage JSON-LD Description in all versions up to, and including, 3.1.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the target page renders a core/latest-comments block with the displayExcerpt option enabled, causing comment content to be incorporated into the WebPage JSON-LD description output in wp_head.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131577
CVE.report.description: The WSMS (formerly WP SMS): SMS Notifications, OTP Login and WooCommerce SMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 7.2.14. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to send arbitrary SMS messages to attacker-chosen phone numbers from the site's trusted sender ID, incurring per-message gateway charges to the site owner and enabling SMS spam or phishing campaigns.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130148
CVE.report.description: The YMC Filter plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 3.14.1 via the 'post_status' parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to extract retrieve rendered grid HTML containing titles, excerpts, author names, dates, categories, tags, and thumbnails of private, draft, pending, and future posts they do not have permission to view. Exposure only occurs when an administrator has configured at least one non-publish status in the filter grid's Appearance → Post Status setting, as attacker-supplied statuses are intersected with this administrator-defined allowlist before being passed to WP_Query.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129220
CVE.report.description: The Everest Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form, Quiz, Survey & Custom Form Builder with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Missing Authorization in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.4 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with everest_forms_create_forms capabilities, to activate any already-installed inactive plugin on the server by supplying an arbitrary slug, triggering its activation hooks and escalating privileges up to administrator level. Exploitation requires that a site administrator has delegated the everest_forms_create_forms capability to a lower-privileged role via the plugin's Role & Permission feature, and that at least one inactive installed plugin whose main file follows the slug/slug.php naming convention exists on the server.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129096
CVE.report.description: The Themify Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.8.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129095
CVE.report.description: The Social Media Auto Poster – Schedule & Publish to Buffer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 6.2.9. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to delete Buffer sync log history for and disclose Buffer sync log contents of arbitrary posts, including those authored by administrators. The nonce used as the sole gate is not bound to any specific post ID, so a nonce harvested from the attacker's own draft editor screen is valid against any arbitrary post ID submitted in the request.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-126701
CVE.report.description: The Themify Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.8.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The wp_kses_post filter applied during save is ineffective against tagless attribute-breakout payloads, as it only strips disallowed HTML tags and cannot neutralize a payload containing no '<' characters; the element_id is then echoed without esc_attr() inside a data-id HTML attribute in template-tab.php.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-125011
CVE.report.description: The Themify Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.8.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-123086
CVE.report.description: The PublishPress Revisions: Duplicate Posts, Submit, Approve and Schedule Content Changes plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.4 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to permanently force-delete arbitrary trashed posts, pages, and revisions owned by any user, including higher-privileged users. The required nonce is trivially harvested by any Contributor-level user because the static 'revisions-deleted' nonce action is emitted in a redirect header on the init hook before WordPress enforces edit.php's capability check, and once obtained it authorizes deletion of any trashed post or revision on the site.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-122223
CVE.report.description: The plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'values[text_shadow_color]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The wp_kses_post sanitization applied at save time does not strip the payload because it is stored as URL-encoded JSON inside a shortcode attribute, containing no literal HTML tags for kses to tokenize, leaving the malicious value intact until render time.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-122221
CVE.report.description: The plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'section_title_tag' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Although the plugin ships a resolveSectionTitleTag() helper that enforces an [h1–h6, p] allow-list, the accordion render path never invokes it, and the wp_kses_post sanitization applied to post_content on save does not parse shortcode attribute text, leaving the malicious value stored verbatim.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-122161
CVE.report.description: The plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'hover_custom_background' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. wp_kses_post applied to post content on save does not parse shortcode attribute text, allowing injected double-quotes to survive storage and break out of the style attribute context at render time.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-119182
CVE.report.description: The PublishPress Tag Groups: Stylish Displays For Your Tags and Categories plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'separator' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.0.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is possible because wp_kses_post applied on save treats HTML-entity-encoded payloads as inert text, but the plugin's own check_attributes() function calls html_entity_decode() on the separator value before passing it to unescaped output, reconstituting live markup at render time.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-119180
CVE.report.description: The PublishPress Tag Groups: Stylish Displays For Your Tags and Categories plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'column_gap' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.0.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.
