The payload bypasses wp_kses_post sanitization on save because it contains no HTML tags — only a double-quote character within shortcode attribute syntax that breaks out of the style attribute at render time.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-133471
CVE.report.description: The Fastcache by Host.it plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 's' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.14 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. This code path is only reachable when both the Light Images feature and the DOMDocument entity-decode branch are enabled (lightimgs_status = 1 and img_processing_entity_decode = 1), which reflect the default plugin configuration.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-133439
CVE.report.description: The Coupon Creator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is only exploitable when an administrator has enabled the 'Disable Print View' option (cctor_hide_print_link), as this setting is required to reach the vulnerable else branch; the default configuration is not affected.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132781
CVE.report.description: The Booking Calendar plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the plugin's 'booking' shortcode in all versions up to, and including, 12.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on user supplied attributes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132089
CVE.report.description: The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not keep a subscriber's secret key out of the redirect it returns after a subscription request when double opt-in is enabled, allowing unauthenticated attackers to confirm a subscription for any email address without access to its mailbox and, when the address already has an unconfirmed subscription, to reset that record with their own details.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132082
CVE.report.description: The RSVPMaker for Toastmasters WordPress plugin before 6.9.3 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before outputting it back in an admin page, leading to a Reflected Cross-Site Scripting which could be used against high privilege users such as admin.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132081
CVE.report.description: The Titan Anti-spam & Security  WordPress plugin before 7.5.5 does not protect or remove the diagnostic archive it writes to the uploads folder when an administrator exports its logs, and names it after the export date alone, allowing unauthenticated visitors to download the Titan Anti-spam & Security  WordPress plugin before 7.5.5's logs, including visitor IP addresses, and the site's system information.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132073
CVE.report.description: The Keywords to Links Converter WordPress plugin before 2.2.5 does not validate a value submitted to one of its AJAX actions before saving it as an option that it later uses in an arithmetic operation on every admin and front-end request, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to make the whole site return a fatal error until the option is manually reset.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132044
CVE.report.description: The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.8.0 does not check that a lesson belongs to the course a course creator is authorised to manage before moving it, allowing a user with the Course Creator role to move lessons out of other creators' courses into their own and read their content.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132042
CVE.report.description: The Keywords to Links Converter WordPress plugin before 2.2.5 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement via an AJAX action available to any authenticated user, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to perform SQL injection attacks and read arbitrary data from the database.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131985
CVE.report.description: The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.13.0 does not verify that a referenced media item belongs to the user, or is not already attached elsewhere, before re-linking it to their own content, and its media identifiers are predictable from public post data, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to take over and delete media uploaded by other users, including administrators.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131984
CVE.report.description: The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.7.0 does not verify that the user is allowed to manage the space it actually modifies or deletes, allowing a user who administers any one space to modify or permanently delete any other space on the site, together with its posts, comments, reactions and memberships.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131983
CVE.report.description: The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.13.0 does not apply the per-link visibility rules of space sidebar links when listing spaces in its space discovery feature, allowing unauthenticated visitors to retrieve the titles and URLs of links restricted to logged-in users or specific memberships, as well as disabled links, for every public and private space.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131979
CVE.report.description: The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict the content type of its lightbox shortcode, allowing users with the contributor role and above to make the lightbox fetch HTML from an attacker-controlled server and insert it into the page unsanitised, leading to Stored Cross-Site Scripting when a user opens the lightbox.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131978
CVE.report.description: The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict which PHP functions a shortcode's filter attribute can call, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to remove WordPress' term-slug sanitization and perform SQL injection attacks through another shortcode's taxonomy term attribute.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131977
CVE.report.description: The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not escape the error message returned when a remote feed cannot be retrieved before outputting it, which could allow users with the contributor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against administrators by pointing the feed at a server they control.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131976
CVE.report.description: The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not prevent placeholders in a shortcode attribute from being expanded with unescaped nested shortcode output, allowing users with a role as low as contributor to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131975
CVE.report.description: The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not prevent format specifiers in a shortcode attribute from being interpreted when building navigation menu markup, which could allow users with a role as low as Contributor to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131971
CVE.report.description: The Payment forms, Buy now buttons, and Invoicing System | GetPaid WordPress plugin before 2.8.63 does not check that the visitor is allowed to view an invoice before rendering it through its single-invoice shortcode, and its payment-form embed page lets unauthenticated users render that shortcode for any invoice ID, disclosing customers' names, billing addresses, phone numbers, line items and payment status.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130894
CVE.report.description: The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not protect its unsubscription actions against Cross-Site Request Forgery for subscribers it identifies from its own tracking cookie, allowing attackers to unsubscribe a subscriber from the site's newsletter by making them visit a malicious page.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130892
CVE.report.description: The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not properly validate the destination of the redirect performed when a subscriber changes their list membership from a newsletter link, checking only that it begins with the site's URL, allowing unauthenticated attackers to redirect users to external sites whose address starts with the site's URL.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130891
CVE.report.description: The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not check that a visitor is really the subscriber before showing them newsletters marked as private, and accepts a weaker subscriber identifier that anyone can obtain by submitting a known subscriber's email address to the public subscription form, allowing unauthenticated attackers who know a subscriber's email address to read every private newsletter sent to that subscriber.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-127002
CVE.report.description: The RSVP and Event Management WordPress plugin before 2.7.19 does not escape a submitted value before outputting it back in its RSVP form when the form is re-displayed after a failed submission, leading to a Reflected Cross-Site Scripting which could be used against high-privilege users such as admins.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-126039
CVE.report.description: The Hide My WP Ghost  WordPress plugin before 7.0.19 does not limit one of its HTML output rewriting patterns to the markup it targets, allowing unauthenticated attackers to inject HTML attributes through a comment author name that execute as Stored XSS for any visitor, including logged-in administrators, on pages that list recent comments.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-125932
CVE.report.description: The Coupon Creator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'metavalue (with metakeyinput=cctor_expiration)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit is possible because the cctor_coupon post type advertises 'custom-fields' support, enabling WordPress core's Custom Fields metabox for Contributors, and the unregistered cctor_expiration meta key causes sanitize_meta() to be a no-op, allowing raw HTML to be stored verbatim in the database via a single AJAX request.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-123663
CVE.report.description: The ProfilePress  WordPress plugin before 4.18.1 takes the role for an account registered through a combined login and registration form from the separate registration form that shares its numeric ID, allowing unauthenticated users to register with the elevated role, such as Editor, assigned by an unpublished registration form.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-121155
CVE.report.description: The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not preserve the escaping of JSON-formatted database values when they rewrite the database during a restore to a new address or server, which could allow unauthenticated attackers to plant harmless-looking escaped markup, for example in a comment author name, that becomes Stored Cross-Site Scripting once an administrator performs such a restore.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-121154
CVE.report.description:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not keep serialized string lengths consistent when their database search and replace processes certain serialized values, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant data that becomes an attacker-chosen PHP object after an administrator runs a URL-lengthening search and replace or a migration restore.

When the replacement changes the length of the text, the declared string lengths inside the stored value no longer match and the corrupted value is written back, so when WordPress later reads it the trailing bytes are parsed as further serialized structure, including an object of a class the attacker named. No gadget chain is known in the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 themselves; further impact depends on classes available from other installed code.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-121153
CVE.report.description:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not keep a serialized value inert when their database search and replace reaches its recursion limit, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant data in their own user meta that is rewritten into a live PHP object when an administrator later runs a search and replace or a migration restore, and is then instantiated by WordPress on a later read.

This is distinct from CVE-2024-10957, whose fix restricted the unserialize call but left this path in place. No gadget chain is present in WordPress core or the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 themselves; further impact depends on a suitable class from another installed UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 or .

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-121152
CVE.report.description: The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not safely process the output of the external database dump tool when backing up large tables, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to store profile data that turns into SQL executed when an administrator later restores the backup, for example to grant themselves the administrator role.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-121151
CVE.report.description:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not preserve long database values byte-for-byte when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a serialized value that becomes a PHP Object Injection once an administrator backs up and restores the database.

No gadget chain is known in the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 or WordPress core, so the demonstrated effect is instantiation of an attacker-chosen class in the attacker's own requests. Exploitation requires the planted data to line up exactly with how the backup is read back, which depends on details of the attacker's row and the database dump format.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-121150
CVE.report.description:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not correctly handle comment-like content found in the middle of a long SQL statement when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber who have stored crafted content in their own profile to have SQL executed when an administrator later restores a backup, and so escalate their account to administrator.

This is a different code path from the backup restore issue fixed in 1.26.10, and it does not depend on the database server's maximum packet size.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120539
CVE.report.description: The Restrictions for BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This is due to the plugin splicing the attacker-controlled request URI into a PHP expression inside a double-quoted string and evaluating it with eval(). Because PHP interpolates double-quoted strings, a payload of the form {${...}} in the URL path is executed during interpolation, so no quote breakout is required and WordPress' slashing does not mitigate it. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server with a single GET request. The affected conditions ship enabled by default and are evaluated before any logged-in check, so no plugin configuration is needed; the site must have BuddyPress and Paid Memberships Pro active alongside this plugin.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-119607
CVE.report.description: The Salon Booking System – Appointment Booking for Salons, Barbershops & Spas plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 10.31.16. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to overwrite arbitrary users' user meta fields, including the _sln_phone and _sln_sms_prefix meta of administrator accounts, and create bookings attributed to arbitrary users. This is exploitable on default installations because reCAPTCHA is disabled by default, causing the booking endpoint's permission check to return true for any authenticated user without a meaningful authorization gate.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-119184
CVE.report.description: The Mapster WP Maps — Mapbox, MapLibre & Google Maps for WordPress plugin before 2.0.7 does not perform any authorization check when saving edits made through its bundled photo-gallery library, allowing any authenticated user with at least Contributor-level access to overwrite the title and content of, and write arbitrary metadata onto, any post, page or media attachment on the site regardless of ownership.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-115226
CVE.report.description: The GiveWP  WordPress plugin before 4.19.2.1 does not properly restrict access to sensitive donor information in one of its REST API endpoints, allowing any authenticated user who owns a donor record, such as a subscriber who has donated once, to retrieve the email address, phone number, name, postal address and company of all donors.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114436
CVE.report.description: The Video Conferencing with Zoom WordPress plugin before 4.7.0 does not check that a requested Zoom meeting's recordings were published on the site before fetching them with the site's connected Zoom account, allowing unauthenticated users who know a meeting ID to retrieve that meeting's cloud recording details, including its topic, share link, passcode when returned by Zoom, and direct play and download links.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114435
CVE.report.description: The Video Conferencing with Zoom WordPress plugin before 4.7.0 does not check authorization, or whether a meeting is restricted to logged-in users, password-protected or unpublished, before returning a meeting's join links, allowing unauthenticated users to obtain the passcode-embedded join links of any meeting, including meetings the site restricts.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114434
CVE.report.description: The Video Conferencing with Zoom WordPress plugin before 4.7.0 does not check that the requester is authorized to join a meeting before issuing a Zoom Meeting SDK signature for it, allowing unauthenticated users to obtain a valid signed join credential for an arbitrary meeting.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-111975
CVE.report.description: The GiveWP  WordPress plugin before 4.19.2.1 does not exclude donors who chose to give anonymously from one of its public REST API listings, allowing unauthenticated users to retrieve those donors' names.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-111067
CVE.report.description:
The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.10, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.10.26 does not guard all execution paths of its database restore process against second-order SQL injection, allowing a Subscriber-level user who has stored crafted content in their own account to escalate to administrator when an administrator later restores a backup.
This is due to an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-108761 in 1.26.9: the fix guards only one of the restore routine's execution paths, and a second path remains exploitable.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-133325
CVE.report.description:
Key exchange without entity authentication vulnerability in Apache Tomcat allowed an unauthenticated node to join a cluster when the cluster was secured with TLS 1.3 and TLS-PSK.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: 11.0.28-11.0.29, 10.1.62, 9.0.124.



Users are recommended to switch to TLS 1.2 and TLS-PSK or upgrade to version 11.0.30, 10.1.63 or 9.0.125 (when released), which fix the issue.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-133958
CVE.report.description: A flaw was found in Quay. Insufficient validation of repository notification webhook URLs allows an authenticated administrator to trigger Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). By specifying an internal URL or a redirect to an internal destination, an attacker can force the Quay worker to issue unauthorized HTTP requests to internal network locations and cloud metadata services.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132660
CVE.report.description:
In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), several SECURITY DEFINER functions in the pem schema of the PEM backend database are owned by a superuser but do not set a safe search_path. Any PEM user who can connect to the PEM backend database can create objects that these functions use in place of the intended ones, and so run arbitrary SQL with superuser privileges. Temporary objects can be used for this on every supported PostgreSQL version, and objects in the public schema on PostgreSQL 14 backends and backends upgraded from PostgreSQL 14.
From PEM 10.6.1, these functions run with a fixed search_path.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132659
CVE.report.description:
In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the row-level security policies on pem.job and pem.jobstep that apply to PEM agents do not limit an agent to its own jobs. An attacker who controls one monitored host, and so its PEM agent certificate, can create, change or delete jobs for every other agent, including the agent on the PEM server. Agents run SQL job steps with the database credentials of the server they monitor, and shell job steps where batch jobs are enabled, so compromising one monitored host can give superuser SQL access to every monitored database and to the PEM backend.
From PEM 10.6.1, PEM agents can no longer create jobs or change job definitions or job steps.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132658
CVE.report.description:
In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the pem_agent role, which every PEM agent login inherits, is a member of the PostgreSQL pg_read_server_files and pg_write_server_files roles on the PEM backend database. An attacker who controls any monitored host, and so its PEM agent certificate, can read and write files on the PEM server host as the postgres operating system user. This includes the PEM certificate authority key, which lets the attacker issue certificates for other agents and act as them.
From PEM 10.6.1, PEM agents no longer hold these roles.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131239
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in Updates data. If another user who can access the System Update Status report selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the System Update Status report does not validate destination, signature, and vendor-product values before inserting them into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and System Update Status (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/system-update-status) in the Splunk documentation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131238
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled certificate values. If another user who can access the Secure Sockets Layer Search dashboard selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Secure Sockets Layer Search dashboard encodes certificate values for the drilldown link but does not escape the values as SPL search literals before inserting the values into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Protocol intelligence dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/protocol-intelligence-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131236
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, an unauthenticated user who can influence indexed event data could store attacker-controlled values in event fields. If another authenticated user who reviews the event selects the View Adaptive Response Invocations or View Adaptive Response Results workflow action from Event Actions, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the action. The unauthenticated user could then access or modify sensitive data and disrupt services available to the user who selects the action.
The vulnerability is possible because the affected Common Information Model workflow actions insert the orig_sid and orig_rid event-field values directly into searches without safely validating or quoting the values.
For more information see About workflow actions in Splunk Web (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.2/workflow-actions/about-workflow-actions-in-splunk-web) in the Splunk documentation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131232
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in vulnerability scan data. If another user who can access the Vulnerability Scan Details dashboard selects an affected value, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the value. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify data available to the user who selects the affected value.
The vulnerability is possible because the Vulnerability Scan Details dashboard does not validate destination values before inserting them into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Vulnerability Scan Details (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/vulnerability-scan-details) in the Splunk documentation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131226
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in Intrusion Detection data. If another user who can access the Intrusion Search dashboard selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the Intrusion Search dashboard encodes data-model field values for the drilldown link but does not escape the values as SPL search literals before inserting the values into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and Network dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/analytics/network-dashboards) in the Splunk documentation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131222
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the edit_modinput_identity_manager capability could use Asset and Identity Management to modify protected saved searches and role capabilities. With this access, the user could obtain full administrator access to the Splunk platform.
The vulnerability is possible because Asset and Identity Management does not validate the app namespace before sending a Representational State Transfer (REST) API request with a system authentication token.
For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Add asset and identity data to Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/asset-and-identity-management/add-asset-and-identity-data-to-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-95824 - Infinite loop in IPv6 Router Advertisement handling when the RA omits the source link-layer address option
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-95824
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 4:56 p.m. | 19 minutes ago
Description :The IPv6 Neighbor Discovery code in subsys/net/ip/ipv6_nbr.c flushes a neighbour's queued packets at the end of handle_ra_input(). The Source Link-Layer Address Option (SLLAO) is optional in a Router Advertisement; when it is absent, handle_ra_input() still obtains (or creates) a neighbour cache entry for the RA source via net_ipv6_nbr_add() with a NULL link-layer address, so the entry stays in NET_IPV6_NBR_STATE_INCOMPLETE with nbr->idx == NET_NBR_LLADDR_UNKNOWN. The pending-packet drain loop was entered unconditionally for that unresolved entry. Each net_send_data() in the drain loop runs synchronously into net_ipv6_prepare_for_send(), which finds the neighbour still unresolved and hands the packet to net_ipv6_send_ns(), which puts it straight back onto the same pending_queue. The loop therefore never sees an empty queue. With a single queued packet it transmits a fresh Neighbor Solicitation on every iteration; with two or more queued packets it rotates the queue with no allocation and no transmission at all. The loop runs in the network RX thread with the global IPv6 neighbour mutex held. An unauthenticated attacker on the same link can trigger this deterministically: advertise itself as a router, induce the victim to queue off-link traffic toward that router (for example by sending echo requests with an off-link source address) while leaving the solicitation unanswered, then send a second Router Advertisement without an SLLAO option. Spoofing an SLLAO-less RA from the legitimate router's link-local address has the same effect whenever traffic is queued for it. Router Advertisements are processed with no authentication whenever CONFIG_NET_IPV6_ND is enabled, which is the default for IPv6-capable builds. The result is a permanent denial of service: the RX thread spins forever holding the neighbour lock, so all IPv6 transmission and every other user of the neighbour cache blocks, and the Neighbor Advertisement that would resolve the entry can no longer be processed. The ipv6_ns_reply_timer work item that would normally drop the pending packets also blocks on the same mutex. In the single-packet variant the loop additionally floods the link with Neighbor Solicitations. The fix restricts the flush to resolved entries (nbr->idx != NET_NBR_LLADDR_UNKNOWN), leaving the packets queued for the NS reply timeout. There is no memory-safety impact.
Severity: 6.5 | MEDIUM
Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-82675
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 4:35 p.m. | 40 minutes ago
Description :The GiveWP – Donation Plugin and Fundraising Platform plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to donor account account takeover in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0. This is due to the plugin not properly validating a donor's identity prior to updating the password of a linked WordPress account. The donation receipt processes an attacker-controlled first name through the V3 template engine and then reprocesses the result through the legacy `{meta_donor_*}` engine, which can disclose the donor's email-access bearer token. The donor-dashboard password endpoint accepts that token by itself and calls `wp_set_password()` for the WordPress user linked to the donor. If the linked account is an administrator, the attacker can achieve full site compromise and remote code execution through standard administrator functionality. A published GiveWP form with a usable gateway, enabled donor email access (enabled by default), knowledge of the donor email address, and an account already linked to the targeted donor record are required. NOTE: This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-82676 to satisfy the administrator donor pre-requisite for a targeted administrator user attack.

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-115407 - Crypto11 Cryptographic Nonce Reuse Vulnerability
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-115407
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 4:10 p.m. | 1 hour, 4 minutes ago
Description :In `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2` versions `<= 2.0.0-rc8` (and the deprecated v1 module paths `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11 <= 1.6.8`, `github.com/ThalesGroup/crypto11 <= 1.7.0-rc1` and `github.com/ThalesIgnite/crypto11 <= 1.2.5`), the `cipher.AEAD` returned by `SecretKey.NewGCM()` passes whatever nonce it is given straight to `CK_GCM_PARAMS` without checking its length against `NonceSize()`, and accepts an empty nonce. On a token that accepts a zero-length GCM IV — SoftHSM2 does — every `Seal` with an empty nonce encrypts under the same IV, reusing the keystream and exposing the GHASH authentication key, which allows forgeries. Separately, `Config.UseGCMIVFromHSM` sends a NULL IV with length zero to the token unless `GCMIVFromHSMControl.SupplyIvForHSMGCMEncrypt` is also set, so the token has nowhere to write the IV it generates: a `Seal` with a non-empty nonce panics after the plaintext has already been encrypted, and a `Seal` with an empty nonce returns ciphertext under an empty IV without error. On the v1 line HSM-IV mode additionally never copies the token-generated IV back to the caller, so the caller keeps its own nonce while the data was encrypted under another one.
Severity: 9.1 | CRITICAL

Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 7:17 a.m. | 40 minutes ago
Description :vulnerability-lookup prior to version 7.1.0 contains two security issues in its web interface. First, the /user/toggle_2fa endpoint accepted HTTP GET requests and disabled the authenticated user's two-factor authentication without requiring password confirmation. Because the state-changing operation was reachable via GET, an attacker with a basic account could embed an image element (or any other GET-triggering markup) in a comment pointing to that endpoint. When a victim with 2FA enabled viewed the comment, their browser silently issued the GET request, disabling the victim's second factor of authentication. No CSRF token was enforced on the GET path, and no password was required to confirm the action. Second, the comment detail page (/comment/) rendered unpublished comments to any visitor who possessed the URL, bypassing the moderation workflow that was intended to keep such content hidden until approved. The API correctly restricted access, but the web view did not enforce the same authorization check. The combined effect allows an attacker to degrade a victim's account security (removal of 2FA) through a single page view and to read content that was not yet approved for public release.

The socket code uses has_current_bpf_ctx() to recognize calls from bpf_setsockopt() and friends, where the caller holds the socket lock and has already been vetted, and skips both. Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring: free the task context after a grace period A task other than the owner can free a request, io_ring_exit_work() running the local task_work of a DEFER_TASKRUN ring for example, or io_do_iopoll() reaping completions. io_put_task() then takes the else branch: percpu_counter_sub(&tctx->inflight, 1); if (unlikely(atomic_read(&tctx->in_cancel))) wake_up(&tctx->wait); put_task_struct(tctx->task); The first line is what lets the owner leave io_uring_cancel_generic(), and on exec it frees the tctx right after. cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-99799 - io_uring/sqpoll: don't wait for the thread to exit
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99799
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 7:02 a.m. | 56 minutes ago
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: io_uring/sqpoll: don't wait for the thread to exit io_sq_thread_stop() wakes the SQPOLL thread and waits for it to exit. The thread belongs to the thread group that created the ring, so a SIGSTOP or the cgroup freezer holds it in get_signal(), and the wake up doesn't change that. io_ring_exit_work() then sleeps in that wait until someone continues or kills the process. iou_exit has 64 slots, so 64 closed SQPOLL rings of a stopped process keep every other ring from being freed, for everyone. Don't wait. Set the stop bit, wake the thread, and let it exit when it gets to run again. The sqd can now outlive its last ring, so give it a second refcount with one reference for the rings and one for the thread, and free it with the last one. The thread can't reach a freed ring, rings leave ctx_list before dropping their reference, and the io-wq hash is refcounted.

Published : Nov. 21, 2026, 11:16 a.m. | 3 hours, 43 minutes ago
Description :Uncaught Exception vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix allows an unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service via a client-selected legacy serializer on binary channel broadcasts. When an application broadcasts {:binary, data} payloads on a channel topic, any client that connects without a vsn parameter, or with vsn=1.0.0, and joins that topic makes those broadcasts fail. Phoenix.Channel.Server.send/4 encodes each broadcast with every subscriber's own serializer inside the PubSub dispatch loop, calling fastlane!/1 with no rescue, and the negotiated Phoenix.Socket.V1.JSONSerializer raises Protocol.UndefinedError on a binary payload. Every binary broadcast on the topic then crashes the broadcasting process and skips every subscriber dispatched after the attacker. For broadcasts arriving from other nodes the loop runs in the PubSub adapter worker, whose repeated crashes restart the PubSub supervisor and empty the node's subscription registry while sockets stay connected. This issue affects phoenix: from 1.5.7 before 1.5.16, from 1.6.0-rc.0 before 1.6.18, from 1.7.0-rc.0 before 1.7.25, and from 1.8.0-rc.0 before 1.8.17.

From 1.7.0 the diff runs in a Task.Supervisor.async task linked to the tracker shard, and Phoenix.Presence.handle_info/2 has no clause for its failure. The shard then terminates, taking down every channel and LiveView process tracked on it and erasing presence state for all its topics. Repeated joins exhaust the restart intensity and take down the application supervisor. This issue affects phoenix: from 1.2.0 before 1.5.16, from 1.6.0-rc.0 before 1.6.18, from 1.7.0-rc.0 before 1.7.25, and from 1.8.0-rc.0 before 1.8.17.

Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 4:10 p.m. | 24 minutes ago
Description :In `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2` versions `<= 2.0.0-rc8` (and the deprecated v1 module paths `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11 <= 1.6.8`, `github.com/ThalesGroup/crypto11 <= 1.7.0-rc1` and `github.com/ThalesIgnite/crypto11 <= 1.2.5`), the `cipher.AEAD` returned by `SecretKey.NewGCM()` passes whatever nonce it is given straight to `CK_GCM_PARAMS` without checking its length against `NonceSize()`, and accepts an empty nonce. Separately, `Config.UseGCMIVFromHSM` sends a NULL IV with length zero to the token unless `GCMIVFromHSMControl.SupplyIvForHSMGCMEncrypt` is also set, so the token has nowhere to write the IV it generates: a `Seal` with a non-empty nonce panics after the plaintext has already been encrypted, and a `Seal` with an empty nonce returns ciphertext under an empty IV without error. On the v1 line HSM-IV mode additionally never copies the token-generated IV back to the caller, so the caller keeps its own nonce while the data was encrypted under another one.

CVE ID :CVE-2026-131167
Published : Nov. 20, 2026, 12:18 p.m. | 4 hours, 17 minutes ago
Description :pretix offloads certain processes to background tasks that are run by a different server to avoid HTTP workers being clogged with processes that take longer than a usual web request. The browser periodically polls the server to see if the task is already finished using a UUID-shaped task ID. Once the task is completed, pretix resumes to the next step of the operation based on the result of the task. The system does however not check if the result stems from the correct type of task. Therefore, an attacker can supply the UUID of a task of a different type and pretix will continue with the result from the wrong task. In most cases, this will just result in an error because the return types do not match up, but in some cases this can be abused to extract objects the attacker usually should not see. Specifically, a vector was discovered that allowed to abuse this for unauthorized access to other people's ticket purchases. The attacker can, however, not control which purchases they get access to.

Description :In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, dolForgeSQLCriteriaCallback() in htdocs/core/lib/functions.lib.php allows account takeover because it strips only a single table-name prefix from a Universal Search Filter (sqlfilters) operand before checking it against the forbidden-field denylist (pass, pass_crypted, api_key). MariaDB and MySQL accept a two-level qualification such as schema.alias.column, so an operand of the form dolibarr.u.pass_crypted survives the check and is emitted into the WHERE clause. A remote authenticated user holding only the holiday read and readall permissions, which confer no user-management or administrative access, can use the resulting boolean oracle at GET /api/index.php/holidays to recover any user's bcrypt password hash and api_key one character at a time, including an administrator's. Because api_key is accepted directly by the REST API as a bearer credential, this yields full administrative control of the application. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-89012, which added only a strtolower() call and did not address prefix depth. The same denylist also omits pass_temp, which stores a password in cleartext, as well as national_registration_number, salary, birth, address, personal_mobile and note_private.

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-129291 - PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-129291
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 3:17 p.m. | 1 hour, 33 minutes ago
Description :PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation. When catch_workers_output is enabled and the epoll event backend is used, the PHP-FPM master can close a worker's output pipe in fpm_child_close() without removing the associated event, and the delayed cleanup can free the worker record while its epoll registration is still active. A later event is then dispatched through a pointer into freed memory. A local attacker who can execute PHP code in an FPM worker can crash the master or execute code with its privileges, commonly root. catch_workers_output is disabled by default but enabled in the official PHP-FPM Docker images. This issue affects PHP versions from 8.2.7 before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.
Severity: 8.8 | HIGH

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-129289 - PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-129289
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 3:17 p.m. | 1 hour, 33 minutes ago
Description :PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body. PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted. This issue affects PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.
Severity: 9.2 | CRITICAL

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-129182 - Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-129182
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 3:17 p.m. | 1 hour, 33 minutes ago
Description :Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown. A fatal error raised while modified INI settings are restored during request shutdown can repopulate the stored fatal error backtrace after the executor has been cleaned up. The request memory is then freed, and a diagnostic emitted before executor initialization in a later request handled by the same PHP-FPM or mod_php worker can access the stale backtrace. The shutdown error requires per-path configuration of max_memory_limit, or of zlib.output_compression together with output_handler (which .user.ini can also set). The early diagnostic requires Apache per-directory configuration or, for PHP-FPM, a PHP_VALUE or PHP_ADMIN_VALUE parameter sent by the front end. This can cause memory corruption and worker crashes, and may allow remote code execution. This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.
Severity: 9.2 | CRITICAL

cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-109555
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 6:16 a.m. | 1 hour, 13 minutes ago
Description :The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted input during database restore and staging reset. This is due to the database importer treating attacker-controlled text beginning with {WPSTG_BINARY} as trusted internal binary data and decoding its hexadecimal suffix into serialized bytes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to plant a malicious serialized object in their own profile. When an Administrator later performs an ordinary database-including restore or staging reset containing that value, and the restored profile metadata is loaded, either during the restore or in a later request, a built-in POP chain can be used to execute arbitrary code on the server. Additional built-in gadget chains allow arbitrary local file read in both WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro and arbitrary file deletion in WP STAGING Pro. The attacker does not require Administrator credentials or a copy of a backup, but exploitation does require the later privileged restore or reset.
Severity: 8.0 | HIGH

FortiGuard Outbreak Alerts.title: Refrigeration Control Systems Attack
FortiGuard Outbreak Alerts.description:
Threat actors are targeting internet-accessible refrigeration management interfaces and industrial temperature controllers, exploiting vulnerabilities, authentication weaknesses and insecure configurations to gain unauthorized access.

The affected technologies include:

- Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC refrigeration controllers.
- Copeland XWEB refrigeration management systems.
- Dixell XWEB remote monitoring systems.
- Other remotely accessible industrial refrigeration and temperature-control equipment.

Following successful access, attackers can manipulate refrigeration configurations, including temperature setpoints, defrost schedules and operating parameters.

These changes can force refrigeration equipment into continuous heating or defrost cycles, resulting in elevated temperatures, spoiled food and other temperature-sensitive products, equipment damage, operational disruption and potential fire hazards.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Armory Castle Attack
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant have disclosed new activity attributed to ARMORY CASTLE (formerly tracked as UNC5221), a suspected China-nexus threat actor primarily targeting VMware vSphere environments. The investigation reveals that the threat actor exploited two zero-day vulnerabilities in separate products as part of the same intrusion campaign.

The attackers initially compromised the BeyondTrust appliance, then moved laterally across the internal network, ultimately targeting the VMware infrastructure. They deployed several previously undocumented malware families to establish persistence, steal credentials, compromise vCenter Single Sign-On (SSO), and access ESXi hypervisors and virtual machine data.

- CVE-2026-102764: A zero-day vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support, exploited to establish initial access.
- CVE-2026-123890: A VMware vCenter Server vulnerability enabling unauthenticated authentication bypass and ultimately administrative compromise.


One particularly concerning aspect is the ability to steal the vCenter SAML signing key and forge administrative authentication tokens, potentially bypassing MFA and impersonating privileged users.

This demonstrates how compromising centralized virtualization infrastructure can expose multiple virtual machines and the workloads hosted on them. The investigation describes a multi-stage intrusion involving lateral movement, privilege escalation, persistence, credential theft, and ultimately, compromise of the virtualization infrastructure.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Organizations operating VMware vCenter and ESXi should prioritize the following actions:
1. Patch immediately: Apply the official VMware security updates addressing CVE-2026-123890. Also remediate CVE-2026-102764 on affected BeyondTrust deployments.
BT26-05 | BeyondTrust
VMware vCenter Patch

2. Restrict management access: Limit access to vCenter management interfaces, including TCP ports 443, 5480, and 2012, to explicitly authorized systems.
3. Enforce network segmentation: Isolate vCenter and ESXi management interfaces from general corporate networks and other internal appliances.
4. Implement egress filtering: Restrict outbound connections from VMware appliances to prevent unauthorized C2 communications and data exfiltration.
5. Audit privileged accounts: Investigate unexpected SSO administrator accounts, authentication tokens, SSH keys, and changes to vCenter access configurations.
6. Hunt for persistence: Search Linux appliances and VMware systems for the identified malware, webshells, suspicious systemd services, and unauthorized SSH listeners.
7. Review SAML credentials: If compromise is suspected, investigate potential theft of STS signing keys and follow Broadcom's incident response guidance for credential and trust remediation.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs is monitoring the campaign and will update this Threat Signal as new threat intelligence and protection information becomes available.
• FortiEDR: detects suspicious command execution, privilege escalation, web shell activity, persistence, and malicious processes on supported Linux and endpoint systems.
• FortiGuard AV & Behavior Detection: identifies known malicious files, web shells, and malware families where supported by available detection engines.
• FortiGuard Web Filtering: helps restrict access to known malicious infrastructure and suspicious external destinations.
• FortiGuard IoC Service: uses identified network indicators to support threat hunting and blocking through supported integrations.
• FortiNDR: identifies suspicious internal scanning, unusual management-plane communications, and lateral movement.
• FortiPAM: strengthens privileged access controls for administrative accounts and remote access to virtualization infrastructure.
• FortiGuard Incident Response: assists organizations in investigating potential compromise, credential theft, persistence, and data exfiltration.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Java4Shell
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-114938, known as Java4Shell, is a critical heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Base64 implementation of the Java standard library.

The vulnerability affects Java runtimes on systems using x86-64 processors that support AVX-512 Vector Byte Manipulation Instructions (VBMI). An unauthenticated remote attacker could potentially exploit the flaw by sending specially crafted Base64 data to vulnerable Java processes, resulting in memory corruption, information disclosure, application crashes, or arbitrary code execution.

The vulnerability occurs when the Java Base64 implementation processes specially crafted input using an optimized AVX-512 code path.

An invalid condition in the processing logic can cause data to be written beyond the bounds of an internal eight-byte buffer, potentially corrupting adjacent memory.

Depending on the application and execution environment, successful exploitation could result in:
- Arbitrary code execution within the affected Java process.
- Disclosure of sensitive information from process memory.
- Memory corruption and application crashes.
- Potential compromise of applications and services running vulnerable Java environments.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Organizations are advised to review the Oracle Security Alerts for the latest vulnerability details, affected versions, and available patches.

On November 17, 2026, CISA issued an alert urging organizations to immediately patch CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell).

CISA recommends identifying vulnerable Java installations, including runtimes embedded in third-party applications, containers, and appliances, and prioritizing remediation of internet-facing systems. Where patching is not immediately possible, organizations should implement temporary mitigations, including restricting and validating Base64 input and limiting unauthenticated access.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Apache HTTP/2 RCE
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-119618 is a race condition (CWE-362) in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 module. In assign_headers(), the module writes to a header table that is shared between the connection thread and worker threads without adequate synchronization. Concurrent access can corrupt the Apache child-process heap, which can be leveraged toward remote code execution in the worker process.

Exploitation requires no authentication and no user interaction. The server only reaches the vulnerable code when HTTP/2 is enabled through the Protocols directive (h2 or h2c). The Apache default is HTTP/1.1, which is not exposed.

Apache HTTP Server is one of the most widely deployed web servers, and this flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker over the network on any instance with HTTP/2 enabled.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Affected versions:
• Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 through 2.4.70, when HTTP/2 is enabled.
• Standalone mod_h2 2.0.8 through 2.0.42.

1. Apply the security update. Upgrade to Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 or later, or install the distribution vendor's fixed package, then restart httpd. Prioritize internet-facing servers with HTTP/2 enabled.

2. Confirm exposure. Check whether mod_http2 is loaded (apachectl -M | grep http2) and whether any Protocols directive includes h2 or h2c, globally or per virtual host. Servers without HTTP/2 are not affected.

3. If patching is delayed, set Protocols http/1.1 and check every virtual host. This removes exposure but is not a substitute for patching.

4. Rebuild containers. Rebuild and redeploy container images that bundle the affected Apache versions. Restarting a running container does not update the binary.

5. Standalone mod_h2 users should disable HTTP/2 until a fixed standalone release is available.

6. Monitor for signs of exploitation. Correlate HTTP/2 request bursts with Apache worker crashes, segmentation faults, or restarts. Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by httpd or apache2, and on new files in web roots or temporary directories.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs is monitoring CVE-2026-119618 and will update this Threat Signal as new threat intelligence and protection information becomes available.

• FortiGuard IPS has released signature coverage to detect and protect against attacks targeting CVE-2026-119618. IPS Signature 60872

• FortiGuard Vulnerability Management (Endpoint Vulnerability): Released endpoint vulnerability detection that identifies hosts running the affected Apache HTTP Server versions, available in endpoint vulnerability package 2.00814 for Linux. Endpoint Vulnerability | FortiGuard Labs

• FortiGuard Web Filtering blocks access to known malicious domains, command-and-control infrastructure, and payload-hosting locations associated with post-exploitation activity.

• FortiGuard Indicators of Compromise (IOC) Service can help identify known indicators associated with compromise and malicious infrastructure.

• FortiEDR provides endpoint detection and response capabilities to identify and contain suspicious post-exploitation activity, including unexpected processes and malicious behavior on potentially compromised Apache servers.

• FortiGuard Incident Response supports investigation, containment, and recovery following suspected compromise of affected Apache HTTP Server deployments.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: WordPress Core Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition Vulnerability
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-119977 is a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition (CWE-367) in WordPress Core that affects the full-package core upgrade process. During an update, WordPress stages upgrade files in a predictable, web-accessible directory under `wp-content/upgrade/`. These files include the `setup-config.php` installer.

An unauthenticated remote attacker who accesses the staged installer during the upgrade window can exploit this condition to execute arbitrary code on the server. According to published technical analyses, the attacker can supply their own database configuration details, causing the upgrade process to overwrite the site's existing `wp-config.php` file with the attacker's configuration. This can allow the attacker to create an administrator account and execute arbitrary PHP code.

The vulnerability has a CVSS score of 8.1. Exploitation requires no authentication or user interaction but is timing-dependent, as the attack is only possible while a vulnerable site is actively performing a full-package core update.

Although the exploitation window is limited to the duration of the update process, the exposure is significant because WordPress sites are widely deployed and internet-facing. Organizations running affected versions should prioritize applying the security update and verify that no unauthorized changes or administrator accounts were introduced during potentially vulnerable upgrade windows.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Fixed versions: WordPress released 7.1.4 on October 28, 2026, with fixes for each supported branch.

1. Block web access to wp-content/upgrade/ before updating. The first update to a fixed release still runs through the vulnerable updater. Researchers recommend denying the path at the web server (Nginx or Apache) and confirming a 403 response before starting the update.
2. Apply the security update. Upgrade to WordPress 7.1.4, or to the fixed release for your branch, then verify the installed version.
3. Clean up staging files. Delete leftover files under wp-content/upgrade/ that the updater did not remove.
4. Monitor for exploitation attempts. Review web server logs for requests to PHP files under wp-content/upgrade/, especially setup-config.php.
5. Review for compromise indicators. Check wp-config.php for unexpected changes, such as a different database host. Look for unfamiliar administrator accounts, unknown plugins, and unrecognized PHP files.
6. If compromise is suspected, restore a known-good configuration, rotate database and administrator credentials, and engage incident response.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

FortiGuard Labs continues to monitor exploitation attempts targeting WordPress Core and the associated attack techniques.

FortiGuard customers should use multiple layers of defense to help identify and mitigate suspicious activity associated with the exploitation of CVE-2026-119977:
- FortiGate Intrusion Prevention System (IPS): Provides network-level intrusion prevention and detection against known exploitation attempts targeting WordPress Core vulnerabilities. https://www.fortiguard.com/encyclopedia/ips/62806
- FortiEDR: Behavioral detection capabilities can help identify suspicious PHP execution, command execution, and other post-exploitation activity on monitored endpoints.
- FortiGuard Incident Response: Organizations suspecting compromise can engage FortiGuard Incident Response for investigation, containment, and remediation.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: OT Refrigeration Control Systems Attack
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

November 9, 2026 Update – Threat Attribution: On November 9, 2026, France's CERT-FR published a threat intelligence report attributing the October 11–12 attacks against industrial refrigeration controllers to Shahid Kaveh, an Iranian cyber-offensive unit operating within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' Electronic and Cyber Center (IRGC-CEC). According to the report, the attack compromised refrigeration controllers at approximately 700 retail locations across France, modifying defrost settings to trigger high-temperature cycles, resulting in significant product losses and at least 15 reported fires. The assessment is supported by shared attack infrastructure, the use of the FOFA scanning tool, promotion of the operation through the group's CyberbanNews channel, and traces of Persian language in the attack infrastructure. CERT-FR also documents the group's broader targeting of industrial control systems, including Schneider Electric, Siemens, and Rockwell equipment, and its historical use of Modbus over TCP port 502 for industrial reconnaissance.

November 2, 2026 Update: A new wave of suspected cyberattacks has affected supermarket refrigeration systems across several European countries, including Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland, and Estonia. Reported incidents involved attackers manipulating refrigeration controls and triggering defrost cycles or raising temperatures, with some equipment reportedly reaching 50°C. Affected retailers include ICA, Coop, Carrefour, Delhaize, Colruyt, and SuperValu. Sweden's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC-SE) confirmed it was responding to incidents involving ICA and Coop stores. However, authorities have not established whether these incidents are connected to the October attacks in France or share the same threat actors or infrastructure. No threat group has claimed responsibility, and no new malware or indicators of compromise have been publicly confirmed.

On October 11–12, 2026, attackers compromised refrigeration control systems at supermarkets across France, remotely manipulating refrigeration settings and triggering defrost cycles. The attacks caused temperatures in some refrigeration units to rise to as high as 50°C, resulting in food spoilage and operational disruption. Affected retailers reportedly included Intermarché, Netto, Carrefour, Coopérative U, Monoprix, and E.Leclerc.

France's national cybersecurity agency, CERT-FR, reported compromises involving Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers, as well as Copeland and Dixell XWEB systems. These systems monitor and manage commercial refrigeration and related building operations. Their compromise can allow unauthorized changes to operating parameters, potentially disrupting temperature control and damaging perishable goods.

Separate research by Claroty Team82 identified vulnerabilities affecting Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers, including:
CVE-2025-41450, an authentication bypass
CVE-2025-41451, an OS command injection vulnerability that can lead to remote code execution
CVE-2025-41452, a web server configuration vulnerability that can lead to denial of service
Danfoss released fixes for the above vulnerabilities, and organizations should update affected devices to the applicable patched firmware.

Additional research by Claroty Team82 and CISA documented vulnerabilities affecting Copeland XWEB Pro controllers, including:
CVE-2026-25085, an authentication bypass
CVE-2026-21718, an authentication bypass that can enable pre-authentication code execution
CVE-2026-24663, an unauthenticated OS command injection vulnerability
The affected Copeland models include XWEB300D PRO, XWEB500D PRO, and XWEB500B PRO running firmware version 1.12.1 or earlier. Organizations should consult the vendor's remediation guidance and apply the appropriate firmware updates.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

On October 12, France's national cybersecurity response team, CERT-FR, issued alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 warning of numerous compromises involving remote refrigeration controllers.

Organizations should immediately remove direct internet exposure from refrigeration controllers and restrict remote administration to secure VPN connections or protected management networks. Review controller configurations, particularly temperature settings and defrost schedules, and apply available firmware updates and vendor-recommended security settings. Change default credentials and replace unsupported, end-of-life devices where necessary.

If compromise is suspected, isolate affected equipment and follow vendor and CERT-FR recovery guidance before restoring operations. A factory reset alone is insufficient if the device remains vulnerable and exposed. Organizations should also segment OT networks from corporate IT environments, restrict access to authorized personnel, and monitor for unexpected changes to refrigeration settings.

Danfoss identifies firmware R4.2 as the fix for CVE-2025-41450 and R4.3.1 as the fix for CVE-2025-41451 and CVE-2025-41452. Verify the correct release against the specific device model.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Linux Kernel Remote Code Execution
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

FortiGuard Labs is monitoring CVE-2026-98432, a critical use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv4 networking subsystem that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code with kernel-level privileges.

The vulnerability stems from improper memory management during TCP connection request processing. Under specific conditions, concurrent operations may access socket-option memory after it has been freed, resulting in a use-after-free condition.

An attacker can potentially trigger this flaw by sending specially crafted IPv4 TCP packets containing IP options to a vulnerable system. Exploitation requires precise timing but does not require authentication or user interaction.

Successful exploitation could result in kernel memory corruption, information disclosure, denial of service, or potentially remote code execution with kernel-level privileges.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

The vulnerability was introduced in Linux kernel 4.4. The upstream Linux kernel CVE team has published fixes for multiple supported kernel branches.

Ubuntu confirmed on November 2 that fixes for Ubuntu 22.04 and newer were available in its proposed repository while undergoing qualification testing. Ubuntu 26.10 already includes the fix.

Organizations running potentially affected Linux systems should:
1. Apply security updates: Install the latest kernel security updates provided by the respective Linux distribution.
2. Reboot affected systems: Restart systems after installing the updated kernel to ensure the patched kernel is running.
3. Restrict network exposure: Limit unnecessary inbound TCP connections from untrusted networks.
4. Filter IPv4 packets containing IP options: Red Hat provides an interim nftables rule to reduce exposure to the vulnerable code path.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs continues to monitor CVE-2026-98432, including developments in exploitation research, vendor security updates, and the availability of security patches across affected Linux distributions.

• FortiGuard Labs will provide additional updates as new intelligence and protections become available.

• FortiGuard Labs has released a Virtual Patch signature (10010015) to protect vulnerable systems against exploitation of CVE-2026-98432. The signature provides protection at the network layer, helping prevent exploitation attempts without requiring immediate changes to the underlying Linux kernel. FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Day Exploitation
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

FortiGuard Labs is monitoring active exploitation of multiple zero-day vulnerabilities affecting Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS), an enterprise remote access VPN solution. Threat actors have chained three vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2026-111357, and CVE-2026-118527) to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution on vulnerable appliances.

According to security researchers, the attacks have been observed since at least October 1, 2026. The activity was initially attributed to a previously unidentified threat actor tracked by Volexity as UTA0576.

The attack chain begins with CVE-2026-104935, an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows remote attackers to execute commands without authentication. Attackers then leverage CVE-2026-111357 to escalate privileges and CVE-2026-118527 to upload attacker-controlled files to predetermined locations on the appliance.

Once access is obtained, observed post-exploitation activities include credential theft, Active Directory reconnaissance, data exfiltration, and network scanning. Researchers also reported attempts to retrieve Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) credentials and BitLocker recovery keys.

Notably, the attackers reportedly deployed no malware or web shells. Instead, they re-exploited the appliance to execute individual commands and manipulated system logs to conceal their activity and evade Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool.

Ivanti confirmed that exploitation affected a limited number of customers before disclosure. CISA has now added all three vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Ivanti Connect Secure appliances running the following versions are affected:
- Version 25.1.1.2 and earlier.
- Version 25.1.2.2 and earlier.
- Version 22.8R2.5 and earlier.

Organizations using Ivanti Connect Secure should immediately apply the latest available security updates.

Recommended actions:
- Upgrade Ivanti Connect Secure to a fixed release. Versions 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6 address the two additional vulnerabilities. Organizations should follow Ivanti's current upgrade guidance for their specific release branch. Do not assume that installing the earlier October update for CVE-2026-104935 provides complete protection. The subsequent vulnerabilities require additional updates.
- Conduct network and memory forensics to identify potential signs of compromise. Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool alone may not identify all exploitation activity.
- If compromise is suspected, follow Ivanti's recovery procedures, including factory resetting affected appliances, rebuilding virtual instances where applicable, and upgrading to a fixed release.
- Reset potentially exposed administrator, domain, and local account passwords. Revoke and reissue stored certificates and reset API keys and other stored credentials.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

FortiGuard Labs continues to monitor exploitation attempts involving Ivanti Connect Secure and the associated attack techniques.

FortiGuard customers should use multiple layers of defense to help identify and mitigate suspicious activity associated with the exploitation chain:
• FortiGate Intrusion Prevention System (IPS): Provides network-level intrusion prevention and detection against known exploitation attempts targeting CVE-2026-104935. https://www.fortiguard.com/encyclopedia/ips/62610
• FortiEDR: Behavioral detection capabilities can help identify suspicious command execution, credential theft, and other post-exploitation activity on monitored endpoints.
• FortiGuard Incident Response: Organizations suspecting compromise can engage FortiGuard Incident Response for investigation, containment, and remediation.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Node.js Brotli Remote Code Execution (Node2Shell)
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the Google Brotli decoder, a component used to decompress data encoded with the Brotli compression algorithm. Brotli is widely used in web communications and is bundled with Node.js through its `zlib` module.

Brotli is an open-source project developed and maintained by Google for lossless data compression. It shrinks files so they can be transmitted faster without affecting the original data.

The vulnerability occurs when the decoder processes specially crafted Brotli-compressed input. An attacker who can supply malicious compressed data to a vulnerable application may corrupt adjacent memory, potentially leading to information disclosure, denial of service, or remote code execution.

The root cause is an error in the decoder's handling of malformed block-switch commands. Under certain conditions, the streaming decoder incorrectly treats an invalid block switch as a request for additional input rather than a format error. This can cause data to be written beyond the bounds of an internal eight-byte buffer, corrupting adjacent process memory.

The vulnerability affects Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0. Fixed versions include 1.0.10, 1.1.1, and 1.2.1, depending on the release branch. The Node.js project has also released patched versions for affected release lines.

On October 22, 2026, Imperva published research demonstrating remote code execution against a vulnerable Node.js build. Public proof-of-concept references are also listed in Red Hat's vulnerability bulletin, increasing the risk to unpatched deployments.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Organizations should prioritize updating vulnerable Node.js deployments and Brotli libraries to fixed versions. Because the vulnerability can lead to remote code execution, systems that process untrusted compressed content should receive particular attention.

Recommended actions:
1. Apply security updates: Upgrade Node.js to 22.23.4, 24.22.1, or 26.12.1, as appropriate, or a later fixed release. Update standalone Brotli packages to the applicable fixed version.
2. Review application exposure: Identify services that decompress untrusted Brotli data, including applications using node:zlib, HTTP clients processing compressed responses, and middleware that decompresses incoming request bodies.
3. Apply temporary restrictions where feasible: Until updates are deployed, limit untrusted Brotli-compressed traffic on affected application paths where operationally practical. Test any restrictions to avoid disrupting legitimate traffic.
4. Investigate suspicious activity: Review application and process logs for unexpected crashes or decompression errors. Correlate anomalies with incoming traffic and runtime versions; these symptoms alone do not confirm exploitation.
5. Rebuild and redeploy affected containers: Ensure production images and bundled dependencies include the patched runtime or library rather than relying solely on host-level updates.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

• FortiGuard Labs is monitoring CVE-2026-111497 and will update this Threat Signal as new threat intelligence and protection information become available. Organizations should prioritize patching affected Node.js deployments and Brotli libraries, particularly where applications process untrusted compressed data.
